For hurtful and vain fables how eager are they ; for empty talk how ready! If the word of life fell among them, they either thrust it from them, or rose and went forth from its presence.
22.6: 6. How many Satans are there among men! And me even me alone every man curses. For lo! The anger of men— it is a devil that grinds him every day. Demons are like wayfarers, who depart if they are compelled: but against anger though all righteous men adjure, it is not rooted out from its place. Instead of pernicious envy, every one hates a weak and wretched demon.
22.7: 7. The enchanter is put to shame with the wizard, who every day tames serpents. The viper that is within him is out of his power; for the lust that is within him he tames not. Secret sin like an asp, when it breathes on him he is scorched. Even when he takes the viper through his cunning, delusion smites him secretly. He lulls the snake by his incantations: he wakens against himself mighty wrath by his incantations.
22.8: 8. I set my stings and I sat and waited: who is long-enduring as I with all? Beside the patient-spirited I sat, and step by step I bewitched him, so that he came unto despair. Him who was ashamed of his transgressions, habits subdued him: little by little I mastered him, till he became under the yoke, till he came in to it and was used to it and did not even wish to go forth.
22.9: 9. I perceived and saw that the long-enduring is he that can subdue all. At the time when I conquered Adam, he was but one. I left him till he had begotten children , and I sought for myself another task, for idleness is not to my taste. I counted the sands of the sea, that thereby I might make my spirit patient, and might prove my memory whether it would suffice, for the sons of men when they were multiplied. Before they were multiplied, I proved them in many things.
22.10: 10. The servants of the Evil One disputed with him, and they refuted his words with their rejoinder. But lo! Elisha brought the dead to life, and conquered death in the upper chamber, and brought to life the widow's son. Lo! now is he in bondage in Sheol. But because the reasoning of the Evil One was very powerful, with their own words he refuted their words. How has Elisha been overcome? Lo! In Sheol he brought the dead to life by his bones.
22.11: 11. If Elisha, who was of small power , was great in might in the midst of Sheol, and if so be he brought one dead to life therein, how many dead then will be raised therein, by the death of Jesus the mighty! Hence even from this consider how much greater therefore is Jesus, than we my comrades. For lo! By His craftiness He deceived you, and you sufficed not to determine His greatness when you compared Him to the prophets.
22.12: 12. Your consolations are of small power, said the Evil One to them of his company. For He Who brought Lazarus to life though dead, how can Death suffice against Him? And if Death conquers Him, it is that He wills to be subdued unto him; and if so be He wills to be subdued, fear greatly, for He dies not in vain. He has wrought in us great terror, lest when dying He may enter in to raise Adam to life.
22.13: 13. Death looked forth from within his den, and marvelled when he saw our Lord crucified, and he said O raiser of the dead to life where are you! You shall be to me for meat, instead of the sweet Lazarus, whose savour lo! It is still in my mouth. Jairus' daughter shall come and see this Your cross. The widow's son gazes on You. A tree caught Adam for me: blessed be the Cross which has caught for me the Son of David!
22.14: 14. Death opened his mouth and said, Have You not heard, O Son of Mary, how Moses was great and excellent above all? Became a God and wrought the works of God? slew the first-born and saved the first-born? Turned aside the pestilence from the living? To the mount I went up with Moses, and He Whose glory be blessed gave him to me from hand to hand. For however great the son of Adam becomes, dust he is and to his dust returns, because he is of the ground.
22.15: 15. Satan came with his servants, that he might see our Lord cast into Sheol, and might rejoice with Death his Counsellor; and he saw Him sorrowful and mourning, because of the dead who at the voice of the Firstborn, lived and came forth thence even from Sheol. The Evil One arose to console Death his kinsman. You have not destroyed as much as you were able. Even as Jesus is in your midst, to your hand shall come they that have lived and that live.
22.16: 16. Open for us to see Him, yea and mock Him: let us answer and say, 'Where is Your power? For lo! Three days have passed for Him, and let us say to Him, O You of three days, Who raised Lazarus, when he had lain four days, raise Your own self.' Death opened the gates of Sheol, and there shone from it the splendour of the face of our Lord; and like the men of Sodom they were smitten; they groped and sought the gate of Sheol, which they had lost.

23.1: 1. The Evil One wailed Where now, is there a place for me to flee to from the righteous? I stirred up Death to slay the Apostles, that I might be safe from their blows. By their deaths now more exceedingly am I cruelly beaten. The Apostle whom I slew in India is before me in Edessa: he is here wholly and also there. I went there, there was he: here and there I have found him and been grieved. R., Blessed is the might that dwells in the hallowed bones!
23.2: 2. The bones that merchantmen carried, or was it then that they carried him? For lo! They made gain each of the other. But for me what did they profit me? Yea they profited each by each, while to me from both of them there was damage. O that one would show me that bag of Iscariot, for by it I acquired strength! The bag of Thomas has slain me, for the secret strength that dwells in it tortures me.
23.3: 3. Moses the chosen carried the bones, in faith as for gain. And if he a great prophet believed, that there is benefit in bones, the merchant did well to believe, and did well to call himself merchant. That merchant made gain, and waxed great and reigned. His storehouse has made me very poor: his storehouse has been opened in Edessa, and has enriched the great city with benefit.
23.4: 4. At this storehouse of treasure I was amazed, for small was its treasure at first; and though no man took from it, poor was the spring of its wealth. But when multitudes have come round it, and plundered it and carried off its riches, according as it is plundered, so much the more does its wealth increase. For a pent-up spring, if one seeks it out, when deeply pierced it flows forth mightily and abounds.
23.5: 5. It is evident that Elisha was a fountain in a thirsting people: and because they that thirsted sought him not out, his outflow was not great. But when Naaman sought him out, he abounded and poured forth healing. The fountain into the midst of a fountain, he took him and plunged him; for in the river he cleansed the leper. Jesus the Sea of benefits, into Siloam sent the blind man whose eyes were opened.
23.6: 6. Gehazi, with the staff that brought to life the dead, was unable to raise the child. And how could the famous prophet have been brought up by the sorceress? We were they that mocked Saul, for instead of one demon whom he questioned, two demons came up and mocked him. From the bones of Elisha learn also of the bones of Samuel; for though Elisha's bones brought to life the dead, the sorcerers could not bring up the dead, the living and sacred bones.
23.7: 7. And though I asked this petition, He who gives all gave it not to me. For though the demons were troubled, by the bones of some priest, or magician or wizard, of Chaldean or soothsayer, yet I was aware that this was but mockery. In two ways I cause men to err: either I make the Apostles to lie, or I make my Apostles like the Apostles.
23.8: 8. The party of the demons lo! It is spoiled; the party of the devils endures stripes: though there be none that lifts the rod openly, the demons cry out with pain; though there be none that fetters and binds, the spirits hang bound. This silent judgment, which is calm and still, and works not even by questioning, the one power that is all sufficing, lo! It dwells in the bones of this second Elisha.
23.9: 9. He gave judgment unto His Twelve, that they might judge the twelve Tribes. And if so be that they are to judge the sons of the great Abraham, this is then no great matter, that they shall judge demons now. And unless they make the crucifiers fulfil the judgment that is to be, by our judgment shall they be proved. For worse than we did they cry out, in presence of the Apostles the judges of the tribes.
23.10: 10. For a wolf was Saul the Apostle, and on the blood of the sheep I reared him; and he waxed strong and became a singular wolf. But near to Damascus suddenly, the wolf was changed into a sheep. He said that the Apostles, are to judge Angels; for by the Angels he signified the priest as it is written. If so be then they are thus powerful, woe to the demons from the strokes of their bones!

24.1: 1. Come, let us hear how they contend for victory: the guilty ones who never have conquered, nor will conquer.—
24.2: 2. Death said unto the Evil One, In the end the victory is mine: for Death is master of the close, as a conqueror.—
24.3: 3. Satan , This were to be Death indeed, were you able: to bring to death a living man, by means of lusts.—
24.4: 4. D ., Lo! I who behold the dead, both good and bad: the righteous who despise you, O Evil One, me they despise not.—
24.5: 5. S ., This dying of the body, is sleep for a time: think not, O Death, that you are Death, who art as a shadow.—
24.6: 6. D ., You, O Evil One, the just have conquered, yea will conquer: but these that have conquered you, lo! I conquer.—
24.7: 7. S ., Even this that you bring to death the just, is not of yourself: because of Adam whom I conquered, they drink this cup.—
24.8: 8. D ., Lo! Sheol is full of the men of Sodom, and the Assyrians: and the giants who were in the flood, who is like me?—
24.9: 9. S ., These, O Death, all of them, by me were slain: I am he that caused them to sin so that they perished.—
24.10: 10. D ., Joseph who conquered you I conquered, O Satan: in the chamber he conquered you but I conquered, and cast him into the tomb.—
24.11: 11. S ., Moses who conquered you, O Death, by sprinkling of blood: he conquered you in Egypt, but at the rock, who conquered him?—
24.12: 12. D ., Elijah who feared you not, O Satan: fled before Jezebel's face, because he feared me.—
24.13: 13. S ., Aaron who withstood you, O Death, with smoke of incense: to him I gave earrings of gold: and he fashioned a calf.—
24.14: 14. D ., You went down to contend with Job, and he conquered you and came up: but I, after he had conquered you, then conquered him.—
24.15: 15. S ., David who by his sackcloth stayed that pestilence: him on the house-top I conquered, who had conquered Goliath.—
24.16: 16. D ., Jehu who destroyed the house of Baal, the temple of the Evil One: was unable to destroy Sheol, the stronghold of my realm.—
24.17: 17. S ., Solomon who snatched from your mouth, a child by his judgment: him in his old age I made a builder of idol-altars.—
24.18: 18. D ., Samuel who in respect of gold scorned you, O Satan: him I conquered, the conqueror, who conquered bribes.—
24.19: 19. S ., Samson who in respect of the lion's cub, scorned you, O Death: through Delilah, frail vessel, I yoked him to the mill.—
24.20: 20. D ., Josiah from his childhood despised you, Evil One: but me not even in his old age, could he withstand.—
24.21: 21. S ., Hezekiah withstood you, Death, when he overcame the bound of life : I misled him and he neglected the miracle, and showed his treasures.—
24.22: 22. D ., John who conquered you, Evil One, and absolved and baptized: I extinguished that torch, which had disclosed you.—
24.23: 23. S ., Simon overcame you, when he brought to life that blessed woman: in a woman he overcame you and by a woman I overcame him and made him deny.—
24.24: 24. S ., Apostles and prophets with one voice, curse you, O Death: Where is the victory of Death, and the sting of Sheol? —
24.25: 25. Your Lord in Sheol you have shut up, O cursed servant: God hates you and also man, hold then your peace.—
24.26: 26. S ., It was the will of Him who gives life to all, that shut him in Sheol: it was you that called Him to this, when you made Adam sin.—
24.27: 27. O comrade of Nabal who in the wilderness reproached his lord: abhorred be your mouth which said to Him, Fall down and worship me!

25.1: 1. Hear, O Freedom, the dispute of two servants: how they are convicted by each other, that they are powerless.—
25.2: 2. R., To You be glory by Whose humiliation Adam was exalted: and by Whose death he was raised, and regained Eden! —
25.3: 3. If then the Evil One overcome you, great is the shame: Death his comrade has convicted him, as being weak.—
25.4: 4. And if again Death subdue you, lo! What reproach: for the Evil One his comrade derides him, as but a shadow.—
25.5: 5. Their dispute is for you a mirror, wherein you may see: that they both are but as chaff, before your breath.—
25.6: 6. Yea and Prophets and Apostles, in their promises: assure you that they like flowers, shall fade at the rising.—
25.7: 7. S ., You, Death, art he whom they hate, the quick and dead: for every combination you dissolve, and destroy.—
25.8: 8. D ., It is not open death that kills, O Satan: your death which is secret kills the sons of men.—
25.9: 9. S ., My name is not hateful as yours, for the angel: showed himself in Satan's likeness to Balaam on the way.—
25.10: 10. D ., How fit is this your name, O Satan: who has erred and made unwary Adam err, from the way!—
25.11: 11. S ., Wander not like one ignorant, and lose your cause: dispute, O Death, if you are competent, for replying.—
25.12: 12. D ., I know that you are wily, O Satan: so that you out of sand can twist a snare.—
25.13: 13. S ., Your disputing, Death, is ended: for he who is worsted: when his words fail and are ended, begins to rail.—
25.14: 14. D ., Among all I am conqueror, and by you am I worsted? Let Adam persuade you whom I have overcome, O Satan!—
25.15: 15. S ., I am he who bound Adam, and cast him before you: the mighty man whom my wiles had bound, you came and subdue.—
25.16: 16. D ., I am he who have been crowned anew, with a diadem in the world: for Adam, chief of the mighty, I hold captive in Sheol.—
25.17: 17. S ., I killed him by secret death, even Adam when he sinned: you, Death, hast slain one that was dead, killed by me.—
25.18: 18. D ., In your desire to conquer, Evil One, you have made yourself hated: for you are Death as well as Satan, and this seems a little thing to you.—
25.19: 19. S ., You have then been silenced, Death, as a weakling: for neither in words nor in deeds, have you strength to stand.—
25.20: 20. D ., It is for your evil you conquer, O Evil One, if you discern, your crown is wholly of shame, if you perceive.—
25.21: 21. I shall be defeated and you shall be cursed, O Satan: it is well for me to be ignorant, and not mischievous.—
25.22: 22. Blessed be the Just One who divided them, though they were quite of one mind: Blessed be the Good One who made us of one mind, when we were divided.—
25.23: 23. I will overcome the Evil One through Your forgiveness, O All-Merciful: and I shall overcome death through Your Resurrection, O All-Life-giver!

26.1: 1. Lo! The Evil One reproached Death, and was in turn reproached: from each and to each and against each, were their taunts.—
26.2: 2. R., To You be glory, Son of the Lord of All, Who died for all: for He was raised to give life to all, in the day of His Coming! —
26.3: 3. S ., Jonah who conquered you, and returned back from Sheol, became my advocate in asking , why sinners were spared?—
26.4: 4. D ., Slander not, O Evil One, the son of Amittai: he showed a face of anger, that they might praise you more.—
26.5: 5. S ., Quite powerless is all your persuasion, O tyrant Death: for there pleases me nothing, of all you have said.—
26.6: 6. D ., For when was the word of truth pleasing to you? A gulf is between you and truthfulness, O lying one.—
26.7: 7. I am righteous all my days, with nought to repent: I am he that rescues from you the sons of men.—
26.8: 8. S ., Proclaim your repentance, Death, you are well come: lo! Saul also among the prophets, great cause of scorn.—
26.9: 9. If you, Death, be justified, then for myself: I cut not off hope, likewise, of repentance.—
26.10: 10. D ., No idol with my Lord have I made, O hater of your Lord! lo! You by dead idols, slay the living.—
26.11: 11. S ., That you, Death, art half of me, I know, and I half of you: if half of me repents, it repents, but I marvel.—
26.12: 12. D ., Your partner am I in share, but not in sin: mine are the slain and yours the slayers, whom you made sin.—
26.13: 13. S ., My craftiness weeps for itself, when I dispute with you: my wiles mourn over me, when I meet you.—
26.14: 14. D ., Workers of witchcraft and soothsayers, with all their offenses: the fire that you kindled in the world, in Sheol I have quenched.—
26.15: 15. S ., You penitent who strainest out gnats, and swallowest the just: the chaste shall rend you, who cry, from within your belly.—
26.16: 16. D ., It is the treasure-house where I keep all the righteous: their resurrection threatens ill to you, who persecuted them.—
26.17: 17. S ., The greedy one who carries all creatures, in his bowels: lo! He casts up to me that I am robbed, of my possessions.—
26.18: 18. D ., Before the stroke lament not, for it has not yet reached you : the day will come when you shall cry out, and I shall hear and rejoice.—
26.19: 19. The fire will come that shall strip off you your very skin: as by the potsherd you stripped the skin of Job.—
26.20: 20. D ., The savour of sloth begins, as if to hover on me; it is then a dream that I ceased, for a short space.—
26.21: 21. It was not that words failed me, and therefore I was silent: it is for the time I grieve, that has passed idly.—
26.22: 22. The hurt done by your speech is very great: would I had not heard it! For my whole mind is intent upon my work.—
26.23: 23. This humankind that is lost, was undone by wandering thought: slothfulness, with negligence, brought it under yoke.—
26.24: 24. The madness of desire bid for wealth, and bought it: contention with boastfulness, were the sureties.—
26.25: 25. With persistence for strength, I wage my war: and if I neglect but a little, my sway is naught.—
26.26: 26. By continual dropping, I clean the rocks: for continual dropping can dissolve even a mountain.—
26.27: 27. Habit even over nature, becomes master: it trains and leads even lions, as beasts of burden.—
26.28: 28. Habit, repose, and increase, with persistence; by these is freedom conquered, though stubborn above all.—
26.29: 29. If its will be firmly set, it breaks the fetters; but if lax, a fragile net, can capture it.—
26.30: 30. If so be that Freedom shouts, we are scattered: but if she be silent we gather together, to mock at her.—
26.31: 31. Let us cease from much speaking, lest it lead to much sloth: with one mind let us assail the wall, and lo! It is broken down.—
26.32: 32. S ., Go and see to diseases, and I to snares: for to me sins and to you pestilences, are great solace.—
26.33: 33. And even though I have paused, I have not paused from my cares: for my will at no time rests, but is ready.

27.1: 1. With Freedom is your struggle, O Evil One: it can cast on you a muzzle, if it so please.—
27.2: 2. R ., To You be glory in whose victory we have gained strength: and in whose resurrection we defy even Death itself!—
27.3: 3. Lo! Again these two exposed each other, how weak both are: Death reminded the Evil One of your mightiness ( O Freedom ).—
27.4: 4. Your fire is in your nest, O Death, and you perceive not: the fate of the departed, to you is overthrow.—
27.5: 5. Lo! Death and the Evil One proclaim your mightiness ( O Freedom ): yea, the Evil One calls to mind your faith.—
27.6: 6. If then these that were against you are on your side: this is a great thing that your persecutors have become your heralds—
27.7: 7. D ., I confess, O Evil One, that as usury: I lay up the King's treasures, till His Coming.—
27.8: 8. S ., I, O Death, rather deny that this belongs to God: this treasure of subtlety, which I have stored.—
27.9: 9. D ., Your coinage is fraudulent, then, O Satan: that into the treasuries of God, is not received.—
27.10: 10. S ., A new coinage do I coin, in kingly wise: lo! My merchantmen bring loss, into the world.—
27.11: 11. God created everything out of nothing: and I created great sin out of nothing—
27.12: 12. D ., Closed and bound be your mouth, Evil One, who art thus bold: to set yourself, lo! In comparison with the Creator.—
27.13: 13. S ., To me, O Death, it is lawful to dare and speak: your tongue, even yours, is a slave, and under fear.—
27.14: 14. D ., A gulf is henceforth between us, O Satan: for madly against your Lord, lo! You assail.—
27.15: 15. S ., Wherefore do you doubt, O Death, of our concord? Be to us comrade and member: and lo! We reign.—
27.16: 16. Come, draw we our pair of swords, against mankind: I secretly, you openly, and lo! We end them.—
27.17: 17. Sin and Sheol they too gave counsel to those two: saying If you be divided, you are undone. —
27.18: 18. See the waters how if dispersed, they run low: but if gathered they gain strength, and thus you likewise.—
27.19: 19. If divided you perish, as the feeble: but yoked together you reign, as the mighty.—
27.20: 20. Love melts down many, as in a furnace: and makes one powerful mass, that overcomes all.—
27.21: 21. In it are wisdom and cunning, and force and power: it is greater far than an image of sixty cubits.—
27.22: 22. Be reconciled, let us assemble and go, against that party: which if it be at one can never be defeated.—
27.23: 23. These things the troublers discoursed, and gathered and came: Your day, Lord, will gather them, into Gehenna.—
27.24: 24. Through Your mercy, Lord, will I worship You, when I have risen: at Your trumpet I will praise Your Son, when I am purged.

28.1: 1. Listen, my brethren, to Death, mocking the Evil One: that caused the head of our race to sin, and its mother.—
28.2: 2. R., To You be glory that by Your humiliation, Satan is subdued: and that Your abasement has exalted Adam, who was abased. —
28.3: 3. D ., Your great nakedness shall be seen, by the sons of Adam; as you mocked his nakedness, when you made him sin.—
28.4: 4. Eve will cease from that serpent, and rail at you: for you, O Dragon, wast he that beguiled her simpleness.—
28.5: 5. Abel will see him, even, Cain, who has come to you: the disciple of his wrath will blame his cursed master.—
28.6: 6. S ., Noah who conquered the flood, as it were death: by the mouth of Ham I laughed at, when wine overcame him.—
28.7: 7. D ., Noah was not harmed, but your garment, wherewith you clothed him: even cursings, he put on, and became a slave.—
28.8: 8. S ., Lot who overcame anger which is, your likeness, Death: to his daughters I gave such counsels, as were pleasing to me.—
28.9: 9. D ., And Lot's wife who was your vessel hearkened, to your counsel: may half of you be dried up, as your whole vessel was dried up!—
28.10: 10. Gehenna be overturned, upon your head: as your malice overturned Sodom, its dwellers!—
28.11: 11. Floods of fire be stirred against you, in the resurrection: who against Moses and Elijah, stirred the people!—
28.12: 12. Let the just mock you at the last, and Joseph rejoice! Whose brethren mocked him, set on by you!—
28.13: 13. Let vapour of smoke come in, and choke your senses: as the waters of the sea choked, the senses of the wicked! —
28.14: 14. Let chaste women also mock you, by whose counsel: the daughters of Midian mocked, the foolish people!—
28.15: 15. Flame be kindled on your head, for Samson's sake: for by a woman you shaved his locks, that lion of strength!—
28.16: 16. S ., Saul whom I conquered by envy, by witchcraft conquered you: for he asked for and brought up Samuel, out of his grave.—
28.17: 17. D ., Slander not the living dead, for he came not up: you were he that came up in the phantom for you were worthy.—
28.18: 18. Let the commandment hang you over the flame, you Evil One! For by you they hanged Absalom, upon a tree.—
28.19: 19. In the fire may you see yourself humbled, among vile women! For Solomon by you was degraded, among profane women.—
28.20: 20. Justice be measured to you, as you inflamed her! even Jezebel who devoured the prophets, you kindled her.—
28.21: 21. In fire may you justly burn, who made them drunken! The two whom Elijah burnt up, when they went up and assailed him .—
28.22: 22. On you also be coals heaped! May he see and rejoice: that Naboth in whom you heaped a pile of stones!—
28.23: 23. Be clad in scorn in the day of judgment, before all beholders! Who clothed Gehasi in a leprosy, by means of your theft.—
28.24: 24. With lightning for a dart be pierced, O Satan! Who in the heart of Josiah, fixed your darts.—
28.25: 25. Sink in the dregs of Gehenna, O Satan! Who sank Jeremiah in the mire of the pit.—
28.26: 26. Daniel escaped from the pit, whither you cast him: may he have comfort in seeing you, in the furnace for ever!—
28.27: 27. Be your wickedness returned on your head, Hater of man: as his wickedness was returned on the head, of Haman your fellow! —
28.28: 28. May the King's Bride mock you, as did Esther: when you beseech her in the judgment-day, to plead for you!—
28.29: 29. Fire released the righteous ones, whom you had bound: a mighty bond be to you, the flame of fire!—
28.30: 30. Be torn in sunder, and may the seven brothers, see your defeat: the sons of Shemuni who by your wolves, were torn in sunder!—
28.31: 31. May fire triumph over your pate, as you mocked: the two heads of Nazarites, sons of the barren!—
28.32: 32. May fire make mock of your head, for mother and daughter: triumphed over John's head, when you maddened them!—
28.33: 33. Flame triumphed over your head, O Evil One: for on the charges you triumphed, over John's head!

29.1: 1. Lo! Death was prompt beforehand, to mock Satan: him who was doomed to become a mockery at the last.—
29.2: 2. R., Glory to You Who by Your crucifixion, conquered the Evil One: and by Your resurrection gain victory, likewise over Death! —
29.3: 3. And for our Lord's sake Death spoke curses on him: who was the cause of His shame, and crucifixion.—
29.4: 4. D ., The fiery pit be your grave, O Satan: who blasphemed the Voice from the grave, that rent the graves—
29.5: 5. My Lord I know, and the Son of my Lord, O you Satan! You have denied your Lord, and crucified the Son of your Lord.—
29.6: 6. This is the name that fits you, Slayer of your Lord : when He appears Whom you slew, He shall slay you.—
29.7: 7. At you shall every one shake the head, for by you the chiefs: shook their heads at Him, the Lord of life.—
29.8: 8. A bruised reed under the feet, of the just shall you be: for through you they put a reed in His hand, Who upholds all.—
29.9: 9. With a crown of thorns was He crowned, to signify: that He took the diadem of the kingdom, of the house of David.—
29.10: 10. With a crown of thorns was He crowned, the King of kings: but He took the diadem of the king, of those that shamed him.—
29.11: 11. In the robes of mockery that they gave him, in those He mocked them : for He took the raiment of glory, of priests and kings.—
29.12: 12. To vinegar is your memory akin, O you Satan: who offered vinegar for the thirst, of the Fount of Life.—
29.13: 13. The hand shall every man lift against you who strengthened the hand that smote Him by Whose hand, all creatures stand.—
29.14: 14. He was smitten by the hand and He cut off the hand, of Caiaphas: the hand of the priesthood is cut off, in the cutting off of the unction.—
29.15: 15. On the pillar again they stretched Him, as for scourging: Him Whose pillar went before, to guide their tribes.—
29.16: 16. The pillar on the pillar, He was scourged: He removed Himself from out of Zion, and its fall came.—
29.17: 17. When they put two beams together, to form the Cross: He broke them, even the two staves, the guardians of them.—
29.18: 18. Ezekiel put together the sticks, the two in one: in the two beams of the Cross, their staves have ceased.—
29.19: 19. The two sticks, as it were wings, bore the people: lo! His two staves were broken, even as his wings.—
29.20: 20. The bosom and wings of the Cross, He opened in mercy: its pinions bowed and bore the nations, to go to Eden.—
29.21: 21. It is akin to the Tree of Life, and unto the son of its stock: it leads its beloved that on its boughs, they may feed on its fruits.—
29.22: 22. Go howl and weep, Evil One, for me and for you: for not one of us shall enter the Garden of Life. —
29.23: 23. S ., Now that you have confessed O Death, come let me tell you: that all this discourse of yours, to me is idle talk.—
29.24: 24. I will go and watch the snares, which I have set: you too, Death, fly and look after, all that are sick.—
29.25: 25. Our Lord has brought both to nought, on either hand: the Evil One shall be brought to nought here, and Death hereafter there.

30.1: 1. Lo! Death for us on Satan, inflicts vengeance: come let us hear his shame and rejoice, for he rejoiced in our shame.—
30.2: 2. R., To You be glory from Your flock, from You: are subdued both Death and Satan, under Your Feet! —
30.3: 3. D ., Evil ones shall be hung upright, but you, head downward: for, reversely, you crucified Simon on the tree.—
30.4: 4. S ., Touching all else I am silent, Death, for my time wanes: Simon himself conjured me, Crucify me thus. —
30.5: 5. Were it the just that cursed me, I had not grieved: the curse of Death unto me, is worse than hell.—
30.6: 6. D ., The shame of our Lord I have not spoken of, it is too great for my mouth: that I should weigh and compare His Passion, with Your torment.—
30.7: 7. Twelve judgment thrones shall He set, for His Twelve: for by the twelve tribes you, even you, shall be condemned.—
30.8: 8. A halter unbought shall you hang you, O you Satan: as that Your disciple hung him, a halter for a price.—
30.9: 9. Haply yon hell in mercy, shall be emptied: and you shall dwell there alone, with Your ministers.—
30.10: 10. Manifold are Your curses, and how shall I count them ? Lo! The sum of all your curses, is on your members.—
30.11: 11. The evil in the fire shall stab you, who made them evil: they shall upbraid you why did you bring us here? —
30.12: 12. Sinners shall rail against you, and haply their threats: shall be worse to you than the torment, of yonder hell.—
30.13: 13. These shall be unto you there, all of them Satans: as you have been to them here, the one Satan.—
30.14: 14. The Watchers shall seize and hurl you down, calling to mind: how through you men hurled their Lord, from the height to the depth.—
30.15: 15. All men will run to stone you, not forgetting that through you the maddened people ran, to stone their Maker.—
30.16: 16. On you, Evil One, from all mouths shall be , the spitting of wrath: for through you they spat on Him Whose spittle, gave sight to the blind.—
30.17: 17. On you, Evil One, from all tongues, shall be all curses: for through you men blasphemed Him, Who opened dumb mouths.—
30.18: 18. Blessed is He Who avenged our wrong, though in silence: and stirred up Death against the Evil One, to fall upon him!—
30.19: 19. Sound we Hosannas, my brethren, as did Gideon: [ Judges 7:18-22 ] who when he sounded, the oppressors, fell on one another!

31.1: 1. O what amazement befell the Evil One, of a sudden, my brethren: when the sinful woman was corrected, and gained Wisdom!—
31.2: 2. R., Glory to the One Who alone, conquered the Evil One; and to Him yea Him be also confession, Who vanquished Death! —
31.3: 3. The Evil One marvelled Where is her laughter? Where her perfumes? Where her dancing and outward ornament, and inward wickedness? —
31.4: 4. Instead of that light laughter, she is given up to tears: She has cut off her hair to wipe the dust, off the feet of Jesus.—
31.5: 5. Naught lasts in her of any doctrine, nor abides in her: from our instruction she has escaped and cast away, all that I taught her.—
31.6: 6. She has denied us and our acquaintance, and even as though: she had never seen me she has blotted my image, out of her mind.—
31.7: 7. The living leaven of Jesus flew to her, Jesus was silent: but she made bold to press and enter, though none called her.—
31.8: 8. She forgot our love of many years, and in the twinkling of an eye: from between me and her she removed it, and set Death there .—
31.9: 9. For instead of laughter weeping delights her, and instead of paint: a shower of tears, and instead of ornament, a sad countenance.—
31.10: 10. Zaccheus I made chief of extortioners, and her I made: chief of wantons; my two wings, Jesus has broken.—
31.11: 11. If so be Zaccheus becomes his disciple, and if so be she: becomes his hearer, henceforth they fetter, my craftiness.—
31.12: 12. Carved images henceforth are a mockery and the carvers: a derision, and the worshippers a laughing-stock.—
31.13: 13. I shut men's eyes that they might not perceive, that they are carved images: Jesus opens their eyes to see that they are the works of men's hands .—
31.14: 14. If Jesus has chosen for Himself preachers, then our preaching: whereof the whole world is full, is put to silence.—
31.15: 15. For lo! The Chaldeans with the soothsayers, and lo! The wizards: with the diviners they are smitten and the priests, with all evil ones!—
31.16: 16. You priests are ended and have given up the Ghost from henceforth, depart you diviners! Become husbandmen, the Chaldeans likewise, shall close their books.—
31.17: 17. If the Hebrews have become His disciples, who by all miracles: were not subdued, who of the nations, shall not obey him?—
31.18: 18. If he begins to set straight the reverse, He brings to naught our speech: henceforth He will not hesitate against us, He who rebukes all men.—
31.19: 19. In that I was worshipped in all temples, our disgrace is greater: than our honour was , for all men spit, upon our altars.—
31.20: 20. Flesh of sacrifice becomes abhorred, into fragments: idols are broken , and carven images burn, under their pots.—
31.21: 21. All our work becomes a laughing-stock, and a ruin: all that we have built, and a mockery, all that we have taught.—
31.22: 22. The secret mysteries that I taught them, laboriously: are about to be spread abroad, on the housetops.—
31.23: 23. Of the Egyptians I was more proud, than of any nation: for they used to worship even, the onions and garlic.—
31.24: 24. Lo! I fear lest even here, where delusion was so great: truth shall prevail that there exceedingly, Jesus may reign.—
31.25: 25. And if when He was an infant, and fled and went down, Egypt marvelled: yea lulled him— this strangler of babes, loved their Babe.—
31.26: 26. Was it a pledge He went down to give her, as a betrother: giving assurance that when of full age, He will also take her to wife ?—
31.27: 27. Pharaoh cannot set his foot firm , for this is no stammerer: that he should deceive Him, and no bondman, that he should lie unto Him.—
31.28: 28. Moses smote and the Egyptians rebelled, and he chastised the people: and the Hebrews rebelled— Jesus is smitten, and gives life to all.—
31.29: 29. This is hard to understand that not by force; lays He His yoke: on the rebellious: He was rebuked, and He instructs others.—
31.30: 30. The spittle of His mouth, wiped off and took away, the shame of Adam: by the smiting of His cheeks, He rooted out our wrathfulness, from His disciples.—
31.31: 31. By the nails which he received, He made me to suffer. I rejoiced when I crucified Him: and I knew not that He was crucifying me, in His crucifixion.

32.1: 1. In wisdom let us hearken to Death, O my beloved: how he accuses us for our weeping, and for our mourning.—
32.2: 2. R., To you be praise Who came down, to follow Adam: and foundest Adam and also in the children of Adam. —
32.3: 3. And rightly perhaps he says, You slay: without mercy and lo! You weep, as though merciful. —
32.4: 4. You have made me as a cruel one, O you murderers: for you slay one another, without my help!—
32.5: 5. While Death was but desiring to come, the sword came before him: let us see then against whom cries out, the blood of the slain.—
32.6: 6. Against you cry out the strangled, who were suffocated: for it shames me of the rope, of their strangulations.—
32.7: 7. They take away from me even my rest, for without me: how could the strangled and the slain, enter Sheol?—
32.8: 8. Lo! Your infants are cast out, as those in Egypt: your sons have you sacrificed to demons, O demoniacs!—
32.9: 9. While Death was but desiring to taste, of your corpses: Cain refreshed me beforehand, with blood of man.—
32.10: 10. While I was but desiring to wait patiently, till Adam should die: before I had power you gave me power, over your bodies.—
32.11: 11. Cain with his sword overthrew, the gate of Sheol: for it was closed and before the time, he first opened it.—
32.12: 12. He by treading made the way of Sheol, without my help: for in the way you have trodden out for me, lo! I walk therein .—
32.13: 13. Nine hundred years I sat and waited, for Adam to die: but Cain not even a day, endured his brother.—
32.14: 14. Robbers upon the highways, are worse than I: I am slumbering while they, are watching to slay.—
32.15: 15. Lo! Your slaughtered in the graves, and your murdered in your ways; and your strangled upon your stakes!—
32.16: 16. If I rebelled against my lord, yea and slew him: who was he that slew these here, said Jehu.—
32.17: 17. And if I Death have taken, your departed: the strangled, the slain, and the slaughtered, who was it slew them?—
32.18: 18. You are Satan to each other, and the Evil One is abhorred: you are pestilence to each other, and Death is blamed!—
32.19: 19. Your own will to you is Satan, yea and a murderer: but of Death and of Satan, all men complain.—
32.20: 20. Poison of Death you give also to drink, each to other: lo! How many Deaths have you, beside me.—
32.21: 21. Wiles, stratagems, yea and snares, sword and poison: how many Deaths from you and in you, lo! Are there born.—
32.22: 22. The judge in the judgment-hall, is a second Death: he slays for secret reward, but I for naught.—
32.23: 23. I have seen bribery and marvelled at it, that ran and outran me: how many slain does bribery, slay, and none perceives!—
32.24: 24. I am ashamed that so unskilfully, I conduct myself: if I take even one corpse, all men perceive it .—
32.25: 25. In the houses weeping and in the streets, also wailing: and even unto the gates of Sheol, they groan over me.—
32.26: 26. Groan over yourselves that you are thus hateful, and you hate me: Sheol henceforth shall groan over you, O murderers!—
32.27: 27. With torture, scourging and fire, yea with stoning: you put to death the sons of men, and you are proud!—
32.28: 28. I am more modest than you and merciful, also reverent: for with reverence I bear away, your departed.—
32.29: 29. On the bed I deal gently, with him that is sick: and quietly I lay him to sleep, for but a while.

33.1: 1. Lo! Death, the King of silence, complains, my brethren: that we have filled his abode with the wailing, of Hope cut off.—
33.2: 2. R., To Him be great praise Who came down to us here below: and suffered and rose again and in His Body, raises our bodies! —
33.3: 3. While we weep like madmen, at the gates of Sheol: hearken what Death says, reproaching us.—
33.4: 4. It shames me, says Death, that you, have overcome me: the half of Sheol suffices not, to contain your slain.—
33.5: 5. For alien corpses together, lie heaped in Sheol: there are two divisions there, the dead, the slain.—
33.6: 6. Whereas I should complain that you have wronged me, lo! You are weeping: you have burst the gate of Sheol, and done me hurt.—
33.7: 7. For you are like an infant, which while yet weeping: laughs again as you also, over your dead.—
33.8: 8. For there is no discretion in your mourning, and no understanding: in your laughter— for to me you seem like, to a weaned babe.—
33.9: 9. One hour weeping and wailing, and after a little: both jesting and wantonness, as of children.—
33.10: 10. For you are unable to become, perfect men: that weep not yea and laugh not, as the discreet.—
33.11: 11. Touching your books we are grieved, that they have toiled over them: who should read them unto you, even the divine Scriptures.—
33.12: 12. The readers are crying aloud, for you are deaf: this their crying proves concerning you, that you are as stocks.—
33.13: 13. For since the reader and the interpreter, are crying aloud: your ears therefore are heavy, or else your hearts.—
33.14: 14. For if there were with you an ear, open to persuasion: it were meet to hear little, and to do much.—
33.15: 15. But because its hearing is closed, whoso knocks at it: the voice returns back to him, who sent it forth.—
33.16: 16. There is no crying with me of mine, I am not deaf: none that reads or interprets for me , I am not dull.—
33.17: 17. The breath that is from Him commands me, sons the God of truth: and with the command there follows, also the fulfilment.—
33.18: 18. With me is no holding back, no turnings aside: I know no arrow even, could outstrip me.—
33.19: 19. But your voices are scorned by me, when you are weeping: over the graves of your departed, in the cutting off of hope.—
33.20: 20. Were it possible or permitted, when you are weeping: I would go forth and tell you , to your faces.—
33.21: 21. I am endeavouring to give, an account of the death: and your voices disturb me, that I err in my count. —
33.22: 22. You nations, let not your understanding, become childish: like that nation whose intelligence, was never great.—
33.23: 23. In which prudence bestows not itself, as in a fool: for its thoughts are darkness, without discernment.—
33.24: 24. For your infants and your sons, in the resurrection: they shall be foremost to come forth, as the first fruits—
33.25: 25. Then after them shall come the just, as victorious: last shall come forth the sinner, as put to shame.—
33.26: 26. For although in the twinkling of an eye, they be quickened: yet is it in order that their ranks, come forth from Sheol.—
33.27: 27. Prophets come forth and Apostles, and holy Fathers: following them in due array, according to command.—
33.28: 28. Lo! That which now is sown, in random mixture: is yielded back in great order, as garden-herbs.—
33.29: 29. For though one in the sowing, should mix all seeds: that which is earlier than its fellow, prevents its fellow—
33.30: 30. And not as their going down was confused, so disordered shall be: their coming up from the earth, for its order is fixed.—
33.31: 31. Lo! I have been against myself, in what I have said: for secret things which you comprehended not, from me you have learned.—
33.32: 32. Instead of the tears that profit not, which are at the tomb: pour them forth in your prayer, in the midst of the Church.—
33.33: 33. For to the dead there is profit in these, and likewise to the living: weep not with a weeping that afflicts, both dead and living!

34.1: 1. Who shall weigh the recompense of Abraham? Whom I marvelled at when he bound, his only son.—
34.2: 2. R., To you be glory, Voice that bringest to life the dead in Sheol: and they have come up as preachers, of His Son Who quickens all! —
34.3: 3. At that time I came forth in haste, to see the marvel: how that his knife was drawn out, against his beloved.—
34.4: 4. I gathered my manifold memories, from all quarters: and I collected my spirit to marvel, at that illustrious one.—
34.5: 5. How therefore can you read, that great story? You have despised the reading of it, in your very ears.—
34.6: 6. The sword of Jephthah rebukes, him that laments: his daughter was to him a mirror of life from the dead.—
34.7: 7. She gave herself for her father, so commend ye: your life to the Father of all, in the hope of your end.—
34.8: 8. In the womb then did you not make trial, of a mystery of Sheol? Yet in Sheol you had more rest, than in the womb.—
34.9: 9. It is stubborn in you to stand up against, my mighty will: for lo! To succour them I take away, your departed.—
34.10: 10. By the king of Moab who slew, his son with his hands: he is put to shame who laments, for the departed one.—
34.11: 11. He was a profane man, lo! According, to what you read: but you are doctors and teachers, as you suppose.—
34.12: 12. He endured, but you are furious, in your mourning: against the will of the Lord of all, while you are weeping.—
34.13: 13. I fear however to let pass, the story of Job: through this feeble mouth of mine, for I am unworthy.—
34.14: 14. So in like manner I turn aside, from mention of their bones: though I praise Him who granted, that they should come to me.—
34.15: 15. Dishonour not your members, by your sins: for in Sheol the bones are despised, of evildoers.—
34.16: 16. Whenever I see the body of one of the evil: I trample on it and curse, even his memory.—
34.17: 17. But wherever I see a bone, of one of the just; I set it apart and honour it, and do it worship.—
34.18: 18. You feeble ones understand not, all my ordinances: with you orders are confused, for you are blind.—
34.19: 19. It is Moses alone that I know, to have honoured like me: the bones of that Joseph whom I magnify.—
34.20: 20. But Moses did such honour, to one pure body: but I to the body and the bones, of all the righteous.—
34.21: 21. Brightly shine the bones of Prophets, and of Apostles: a lamp to me in darkness, are all the righteous.—
34.22: 22. I worship Him Who lightens for me, the darkness of Sheol: the splendour of Moses who was so great, was as the sun to me.

35.1: 1. O feeble ones, why do you weep over your dead: who in death are at rest from sorrows and sins?—
35.2: 2. R., Glory to Him Who endured all, for the sake of all men: yea tasted death for the sake of all, to bring all to life —
35.3: 3. I reveal unto you, that even Satan, though much content: at your weeping, yet laughs much, at your mourning.—
35.4: 4. In mockery he winks at me and nods to me, as a jester: Come let us laugh at sinners, for lo! They are mad. —
35.5: 5. Truly they have given up remembrance of that fire, which I have hidden for them: and lo! The fools are drunken with weeping, for their departed.—
35.6: 6. Instead of weeping as though, without provision: I had plundered and sent forth their dead, lo! They are mad.—
35.7: 7. The souls of the evil are to be afflicted, till the judgment day: and these weep over the graves, like to madmen.—
35.8: 8. They care not for their own sins, that haply tomorrow: they must go in shame of face, to join their dead.—
35.9: 9. And thus shall all be put to shame alike, family by family: in Sheol the wretches shall repent without avail.—
35.10: 10. Leave the drunken and the madman, until that day: wherein each shall shake off his wine wherewith he was maddened.—
35.11: 11. I will go to gather them, like children: that they may play the wanton and the madman, until they perish.—
35.12: 12. Lo! I have revealed to you the mystery, the secret of my comrade: go forth therefore, depart, amend, in repentance.—
35.13: 13. Leave me, I too will depart, I will see to my affairs: that with open face I may give my account to my Lord.—
35.14: 14. I know that the wind as it blew, has borne away my words: for you are the same whom I, ofttimes have proved.—
35.15: 15. I remember Jeremiah how he, compared boldness: to the Indian who changes not his skin , though it is of freedom.—
35.16: 16. For this too belongs to it, even to freedom: that it binds itself by the will, as though by nature.—
35.17: 17. For so powerful is the will, in them that are free: that it may be likened to nature, through its workings.

36.1: 1. Man , O Death, despise it not, that image of Adam: which like a seed is committed to earth, till the Resurrection.—
36.2: 2. R., To you be glory Who descended and plunge, after Adam: and draw him out from the depths of Sheol, and bring him into Eden! —
36.3: 3. Death , I marvel at this seed, and at your words: for lo! After five thousand years, it springs not yet.—
36.4: 4. M. , Its present state passes away, as winter does : and as a handful of grain it comes in the resurrection, to the garner of life.—
36.5: 5. D ., That there is vintage-time, lo! I know, but I have not seen: the dead at any time sown, or yet reaped.—
36.6: 6. M ., There is coming a reaping, O Death, that will leave you bare: and the Watchers shall go forth as reapers, and make you desolate.—
36.7: 7. D ., When did I become husbandman, instead of vine-dresser? Who has turned Sheol the wine-press, into a tilled field?—
36.8: 8. M ., Does not the seed then teach you, which decays and dies: and is cut off from hope, yet from the rain, recovers hope?—
36.9: 9. D ., A dream have you seen you feeble ones, of life from the dead: for in waking time the resurrection, you do not see.—
36.10: 10. M ., Your drowsiness hinders you, that you see not: the multitudes of mysteries which cry aloud, of the resurrection.—
36.11: 11. D ., I know that seeds come to life, but I have not seen: bones that grew in Sheol, and sprang and came up.—
36.12: 12. M ., All your discourse is like yourself, for lo! Ezekiel: has taught you how in the valley, the dead come to life.—
36.13: 13. D ., Trees have I seen how in summer, they put on their garments: but bones in their nakedness, are cast into Sheol.—
36.14: 14. M ., Moses broke by his splendour, your heart, O Death: the son of Adam has regained and put on, the glory of Adam.—
36.15: 15. D. , Our law in Sheol is this, to keep silence: for you are words and for me deeds, O feeble ones.—
36.16: 16. M ., How are the aged passed over if you be vinedresser? He Who hindered you from taking their lives, the same quickens all.—
36.17: 17. The babe in the womb confutes you, which is as buried there: to me it proclaims life from the dead, but to you despoiling.—
36.18: 18. The despised flower despises you, for it is shut up and passed over: yet though lost it is not lost, but blossoms again.—
36.19: 19. The chick cries out from the egg, wherein it is buried: and the graves are rent by a Voice, and the body arises.—
36.20: 20. For a body too is the chick, that is in the egg: lo! Its body to our body proclaims, the life from the dead.—
36.21: 21. With the locust your plea is overthrown, and ended, O Death: for in coming forth from the dust it teaches, the life from the dead.—
36.22: 22. D. , I had been content if already, the resurrection had been: for the day of resurrection had disturbed me less, than your judgments.—
36.23: 23. Merciful is the Son of the Highest, yea good and just: and will not harshly avenge on me, the death of Adam.—
36.24: 24. Have you then no understanding, to perceive this: that your father laid on you, this retribution?

37.1: 1. Hold your peace, O mortals (said Death), a little while: and be like me who am so silent, in the midst of Sheol.—
37.2: 2. R., To You be glory, Watcher, that came down, after them that slept: and utter the voice from the Tree, and waken them! —
37.3: 3. You are grieving, yea, weeping, for him that has gone: as though he came to grind for me, the mill in Sheol.—
37.4: 4. Great is the peace I give, unto the wearied: I wax not weary as you, nor weary them.—
37.5: 5. I hear all manner of curses, from thankless men: the sons of Adam are like Adam, who was thankless to his Lord.—
37.6: 6. Contrary one to the other are your voices, and your doings: with your voices you weep and in your doings, you fight daily.—
37.7: 7. I heard weeping and I thought to myself, that none labours: I saw toiling and I thought to myself, that no man dies.—
37.8: 8. The struggles of man made me think, that he is not mortal: his great weeping made me think, that tomorrow he is not.—
37.9: 9. Hear and let me be your counsellor, if you be willing: for these two, these burdens, are very bitter.—
37.10: 10. Cease a little while from this toil, and from this weeping: toil and weep as mortals, who tomorrow vanish.—
37.11: 11. You are frantic with weeping, for your departed: and you struggle in toiling, for your possessions.—
37.12: 12. It is well with the infants that die, and blessed are they: for they are freed from the misery, whereunto you are cast.—
37.13: 13. Allow me to go to Sheol, and there to say: Happy are you silent dead, how tranquil are you! —
37.14: 14. Hear the conclusion of our own words, If there be a resurrection: weep not, neither labour as though strangers.—
37.15: 15. You straggle as one who was to live, here forever: and you weep as one who never, should rise again.—
37.16: 16. Hear my words, if there be with you place for hearing: and prepare you provision that when I call you may answer.—
37.17: 17. For I hearken even I, to Him that calls me: and will restore your bodies, with your treasures.—
37.18: 18. Let there be peace between us, until that day: and when you come forth I will cry and say, Depart in peace! —
37.19: 19. Come, you and I even now, shall give glory: to Him that brings to death and to life, that He may give aid.—
37.20: 20. Praise from us all be to you, O Lord, the living Sacrifice! Who by the sacrifice of Your Body hast given life to quick and dead.—
37.21: 21. Praise to Him Who clothed Himself in our body, and died and rose again: He died in us and we live in Him, blessed be He Who sent Him!

38.1: 1. Come, let us hear how Death convicts the People: that harsher than Death was their sword, against the just.—
38.2: 2. R., To You be glory, Who by Your sacrifice, hast redeemed our disgrace: and Whose death was instead of all deaths, that You might raise all! —
38.3: 3. It was not Death indeed that crucified Jesus, but it was the People: how hateful then the People, that are yet more hateful than I!—
38.4: 4. Into the pit they cast Jeremiah, the miry pit : but I in Sheol allotted, honour to his bones.—
38.5: 5. Naboth they bruised to death with stones, as though he were a dog: how good am I who have never stoned, even a dog!—
38.6: 6. The Hebrew women in famine, ate their children: Sheol is good who delivers and gives them up, without difficulty.—
38.7: 7. To the widow I gave her son, by the hand of Elijah: to the Shunamite her beloved, by the hand of Elisha.—
38.8: 8. The Hebrew women in greed, ate their children: Sheol gave up the dead and learned, to fast soberly.—
38.9: 9. Sheol was not indeed Sheol, but its semblance: Jezebel was the true Sheol, who devoured the just.—
38.10: 10. The sons of the prophets and the prophets, she slew and cast down: to heaven Elijah escaped, from her fury.—
38.11: 11. How many deaths instead of one Death, were among the People! And how many Sheols instead of one, were there also!—
38.12: 12. Samaria and Jezrael her daughters, in Israel: and Zion and Jerusalem her sister, in Judea.—
38.13: 13. Prophets and just men in Judea, and in Israel: in these two abysses, they were drowned.—
38.14: 14. Why then is Sheol hated, and she alone: though there be many that are hateful, rather than she?—
38.15: 15. The dead of the men of Judah, to me are right hateful: yea, abhorred by me are their bones, in the midst of Sheol.—
38.16: 16. Would that then I had a way to cast them out: to cast their bones thence from Sheol, for they cause her to rot.—
38.17: 17. I wonder at the Holy Spirit, that He thus dwelt: in the midst of a People whose savour stank, as their conversation.—
38.18: 18. Onions and garlic are the heralds of their doings: as is the food so is the understanding, of this defiled people.—
38.19: 19. Through the supplication of all that bow, and worship Your Father: have mercy on Your worshipper, who is thankless for Your love.—
38.20: 20. From Hebrews and Aramæans, and also from the Watchers: to You be praise and through You to Your Father, be also glory!—
38.21: 21. For that I have a mouth to Death, who is without mouth: may the Son Who is all mouths, hold back my offense from His Father!

39.1: 1. Man. , O, Death, be not boastful, over the just: the sons of your Lord who at His command, come to dwell with you .—
39.2: 2. R., To you be glory that by Your command, Death has reigned: and by Your Resurrection has been humbled to low estate! —
39.3: 3. Death. , Herein am I exceeding great, according to your saying: that though I be bond-man I trample on them that are free.—
39.4: 4. M ., Adam was chosen and ruler, and under his yoke: you, Death, and the Evil One, your fellow, became bondmen.—
39.5: 5. D ., This is our pride that lo! The slaves have become lords: Death, and Satan, his fellow, have trampled on Adam.—
39.6: 6. M ., Lo! The humbling of you and your fellow, accurst servants! How Enoch trampled on you both, and rose aloft and reigned.—
39.7: 7. D ., If so be Enoch made me grieve, yet have I comfort for on Noah's dust in Sheol, lo! I trample.—
39.8: 8. M ., Tremble, O Death, before man, for though a servant, the yoke of his dominion reigns on all creatures.—
39.9: 9. D ., I rejoice then that they are no mean foes that I have overcome: for according to the greatness of the vanquished, he is great that overcomes.—
39.10: 10. M ., Well does your voice sing triumph, O Death, over the just: for Enoch and Elijah have broken your pair of wings.—
39.11: 11. D ., I know how to weigh my sorrows with my comforts: in place of two, lo! Many have come and coming.—
39.12: 12. M ., All that have come and coming to you dwell as sojourners, and depart from your abode as Lazarus.—
39.13: 13. D ., This your saying hurts me not, rather it heals me: for Lazarus who rebelled against me, I again subdued.—
39.14: 14. M ., Make answer, O Death, and argue what constrained him, to be raised unless it were a mystery, showing forth his resurrection.—
39.15: 15. D ., You are famous in arguing as idle ones, while I labour in my task to discern and perform—
39.16: 16. M ., You were well prepared for argument, what has checked you? The truth of our resurrection has constrained you by its reputations.—
39.17: 17. D ., You have made me hated by you, though I be not hateful: I am he that gives rest to your aged, and your afflicted.—
39.18: 18. You have made me as one that troubles, O you mortals: Adam brought death upon you, and I bear the blame.—
39.19: 19. Gently will I expose you, for I am a slave, and you are they that by your sins have made me king.—
39.20: 20. The will of Adam roused me for I was at rest: I was dead and you quickened me, that you might die by me.—
39.21: 21. I accuse the lying ones, who slew and denied it: for Adam slew himself and charges me.—
39.22: 22. The beginning of strife was the accursed serpent which has rightly been crippled: which crept, entered, and set enmity between me and you.—
39.23: 23. Satan is passed by and it is against me that you are roused: go, strive with the Evil One who made you transgress.—
39.24: 24. He is my comrade and I deny it not, but though he be much hated, what need that I be blamed for him. I deny him henceforth.—
39.25: 25. Hearken to my words, O mortals, and I will console you: I have afflicted you and I confess the life from the dead.—
39.26: 26. For there begins to steal into my ears a voice of preparation: of the trumpet that holds itself ready to sound.—
39.27: 27. Hear my words and put much oil into your lamps: for hindrance from my part there is none for you.—
39.28: 28. Yet , Know that even although I have said these things, dear is the sound of your voice in the solitude of Sheol.—
39.29: 29. For man has been weighed by me, and great is his peace: for snakes and fishes and birds come to meet him.—
39.30: 30. But it is a marvel that to the Watchers, too, his converse is dear: yea, the Evil One in Gehenna, desires his presence.—
39.31: 31. You shall have life from the dead, O you mortals, and I who am bereft shall be bereft in the midst of Sheol.—
39.32: 32. Let praise ascend from all to You Who quickenest all, and from every quarter gatherest the dust of Adam!

2.1: 1. Whereunto are you like? Let your stillness speak to one that hears; with silent mouth speak with us: for whoso hears the stammerings of your silence, to him your type utters its silent cry concerning our Redeemer.
2.2: Your mother is a virgin of the sea; though he took her not [to wife]: she fell into his bosom, though he knew her not; she conceived you near him, though he did not know her. Do thou, that are a type, reproach the Jewish women that have you hung upon them. You are the only progeny of all forms which art like to the Word on High, Whom singly the Most High begot. The engraven forms seem to be the type of created things above. This visible offspring of the invisible womb is a type of great things. Your goodly conception was without seed, and without wedlock was your pure generation, and without brethren was your single birth.
2.3: Our Lord had brethren and yet not brethren, since He was an Only-Begotten. O solitary one, you type exact of the Only-Begotten! There is a type of yours in the crown of kings, [wherein] you have brothers and sisters.
2.4: Goodly gems are your brethren, with beryls and unions as your companions: may gold be as it were your kinsman, may there be unto the King of kings a crown from your well-beloved ones! When you came up from the sea, that living tomb, you cried out. Let me have a goodly assemblage of brethren, relatives, and kinsmen. As the wheat is in the stalk, so you are in the crown with princes: and it is a just restoration to you, as if of a pledge, that from that depth you should be exalted to a goodly eminence. Wheat the stalk bears in the field; you the head of the king upon his chariot carries about.
2.5: O daughter of the water, who hast left sea, wherein you were born, and art gone up to the dry land, wherein you are beloved: for men have loved and seized and adorned themselves with you, like as they did that Offspring Whom the Gentiles loved and crowned themselves withal.
2.6: It is by the mystery of truth that Leviathan is trodden down of mortals: the various put him off, and put on Christ. In the sacrament of oil did the Apostles steal You away, and came up. They snatched their souls from his mouth, bitter as it was.
2.7: Your Nature is like a silent lamb in its sweetness, of which if a man is to lay hold, he lifts it in a crucial form by its ears, as it was on Golgotha. He cast out abundantly all His gleams upon them that looked upon Him.
2.8: 2. Shadowed forth in your beauty is the beauty of the Son, Who clothed Himself with suffering when the nails passed through Him. The awl passed in you since they handled you roughly, as they did His hands; and because He suffered He reigned, as by your sufferings your beauty increased.
2.9: And if they showed no pity upon you, neither did they love you: still suffer as you might, you have come to reign! Simon Peter showed pity on the Rock; whoso has smitten it, is himself thereby overcome; it is by reason of Its suffering that Its beauty has adorned the height and the depth.

3.1: 1. You do not hide yourself in your bareness, O pearl! With the love of you is the merchant ravished also, for he strips off his garments; not to cover you, [seeing] your clothing is your light, your garment is your brightness, O you that are bared!
3.2: You are like Eve who was clothed with nakedness. Cursed be he that deceived her and stripped her and left her. The serpent cannot strip off your glory. In the mysteries whose type you are, women are clothed with Light in Eden.
3.3: 2. Very glistening are the pearls of Ethiopia, as it is written, Who gave you to Ethiopia [the land] of black men. He that gave light to the Gentiles, both to the Ethiopians and unto the Indians did His bright beams reach.
3.4: The eunuch of Ethiopia upon his chariot [ Acts 8:27 ] saw Philip: the Lamb of Light met the dark man from out of the water. While he was reading, the Ethiopian was baptised and shone with joy, and journeyed on!
3.5: He made disciples and taught, and out of black men he made men white. And the dark Ethiopic women became pearls for the Son; He offered them up to the Father, as a glistening crown from the Ethiopians.
3.6: 3. The Queen of Sheba [ 1 Kings 10:1 ] was a sheep that had come into the place of wolves; the lamp of truth did Solomon give her, who also married her when he fell away. She was enlightened and went away, but they were dark as their manner was.
3.7: The bright spark which went down home with that blessed [Queen], held on its shining amid the darkness, till the new Day-spring came. The bright spark met with this shining, and illumined the place.
3.8: 4. There are in the sea various fishes of many cubits, and with all their greatness they are very small; but by your littleness the crown is made great, like as the Son, by whose littleness Adam was made great.
3.9: For the head is your crown intended: for the eye your beauty, for the ear your goodliness. Come up from the sea, you neighbour to the dry land, and come and sojourn by the [seat of] hearing. Let the ear love the word of life as it loves you!
3.10: In the ear is the word, and without it is the pearl. Let it as being warned by you, by you get wisdom, and be warned by the word of truth. Be its mirror: the beauty of the Word in your own beauty shall it see: in you it shall learn how precious is the Word on High! The ear is the leaf: the flesh is the tree, and you in the midst of it are a fruit of light, and to the womb that brings forth Light, you are a type that points.
3.11: You He used as a parable of that kingdom, O pearl! As He did the virgins that entered into it, five in number, clothed with the light of their lamps! To you are those bright ones like, you that are clad in light!
3.12: 5. Who would give a pearl to the daughter of the poor? For when it hangs on her, it becomes her not. Gain without price that faith, all of which becomes all the limbs of men. But for no gold would a lady exchange her pearl.
3.13: It were a great disgrace if you should throw your pearl away into the mire for nought!
3.14: In the pearl of time let us behold that of eternity; for it is in the purse, or in the seal, or in the treasury. Within the gate there are other gates with their locks and keys. Your pearl has the High One sealed up as taking account of all.

4.1: 1. The thief gained the faith which gained him, [ Luke 22:42 ] and brought him up and placed him in paradise. He saw in the Cross a tree of life; that was the fruit, he was the eater in Adam's stead.
4.2: The fool, who goes astray, grazes the faith, as it were an eye, [ Zechariah 2:8 ] by all manner of questions. The probing of the finger blinds the eye, and much more does that prying blind. the faith.
4.3: For even the diver pries not into his pearl. In it do all merchants rejoice without prying into whence it came; even the king who is crowned therewith does not explore it.
4.4: 2. Because Balaam was foolish, a foolish beast in the ass spoke with him, because he despised God Who spoke with him. You too let the pearl reprove in the ass's stead.
4.5: The people that had a heart of stone, by a Stone He set at nought, [ Matthew 21:42 ] for lo, a stone hears words. Witness its work that has reproved them; and you, you deaf ones, let the pearl reprove today.
4.6: With the swallow [ Jeremiah 8:7 ] and the crow did He put men to shame; with the ox, yea with the ass, [ Isaiah 1:3 ] did He put them to shame; let the pearl reprove now, O you birds and things on earth and things below.
4.7: 3. Not as the moon does your light fill or wane; the Sun whose light is greater than all, lo! Of Him it is that a type is shadowed out in your little compass. O type of the Son, one spark of Whom is greater than the sun!—
4.8: The pearl itself is full, for its light is full; neither is there any cunning worker who can steal from it; for its wall is its own beauty, yea, its guard also! It lacks not, since it is entirely perfect.
4.9: And if a man would break you to take a part from you, you are like the faith which with the heretics perishes, seeing they have broken it in pieces and spoiled it: for is it any better than this to have the faith scrutinised?
4.10: The faith is an entire nature that may not be corrupted. The spoiler gets himself mischief by it: the heretic brings ruin on himself thereby. He that chases the light from his pupils blinds himself.
4.11: Fire and air are divided when sundered. Light alone, of all creatures, as its Creator, is not divided; it is not barren, for that it also begets without losing thereby.
4.12: 4. And if a man thinks that you are framed [by art] he errs greatly; your nature proclaims that you, as all stones, are not the framing of art; and so you are a type of the Generation which no making framed.
4.13: Your stone flees from a comparison with the Stone [which is] the Son. For your own generation is from the midst of the deep, that of the Son of your Creator is from the highest height; He is not like you, in that He is like His Father.
4.14: And as they tell, two wombs bare you also. You came down from on high a fluid nature; you came up from the sea a solid body. By means of your second birth you showed your loveliness to the children of men.
4.15: Hands fixed you, when you were embodied, into your receptacles; for you are in the crown as upon a cross, and in a coronet as in a victory; you are upon the ears, as if to fill up what was lacking; you extend over all.

5.1: 1. O gift that camest up without price [ Isaiah 55:1 ] with the diver! You laid hold upon this visible light, that without price rises for the children of men: a parable of the hidden One that without price gives the hidden Dayspring!
5.2: And the painter too paints a likeness of you with colours. Yet by you is faith painted in types and emblems for colours, and in the place of the image by you and your colours is your Creator painted.
5.3: O you frankincense without smell, who breathes types from out of you! You are not to be eaten, yet you give a sweet smell unto them that hear you! You are not to be drunk, yet by your story, a fountain of types are you made unto the ears!
5.4: 2. It is you which are great in your littleness, O pearl! Small is your measure and little your compass with your weight; but great is your glory: to that crown alone in which you are placed, there is none like.
5.5: And who has not perceived of your littleness, how great it is; if one despises you and throws you away, he would blame himself for his clownishness, for when he saw you in a king's crown he would be attracted to you.
5.6: 3. Men stripped their clothes off and dived and drew you out, pearl! It was not kings that put you before men, but those naked ones who were a type of the poor and the fishers and the Galileans.
5.7: For clothed bodies were not able to come to you; they came that were stript as children; they plunged their bodies and came down to you; and you much desired them, and you aided them who thus loved you.
5.8: Glad tidings did they give for you: their tongues before their bosoms did the poor [fishers] open, and produced and showed the new riches among the merchants: upon the wrists of men they put you as a medicine of life.
5.9: 4. The naked ones in a type saw your rising again by the sea-shore; and by the side of the lake they, the Apostles of a truth, saw the rising again of the Son of your Creator. By you and by your Lord the sea and the lake were beautified.
5.10: The diver came up from the sea and put on his clothing; and from the lake too Simon Peter came up swimming and put on his coat; [ John 21:7 ] clad as with coats, with the love of both of you, were these two.
5.11: 5. And since I have wandered in you, pearl, I will gather up my mind, and by having contemplated you, would become like you, in that you are all gathered up into yourself; and as you in all times are one, one let me become by you!
5.12: Pearls have I gathered together that I might make a crown for the Son in the place of stains which are in my members. Receive my offering, not that You are shortcoming; it is because of my own shortcoming that I have offered it to You. Whiten my stains!
5.13: This crown is all spiritual pearls, which instead of gold are set in love, and instead of ouches in faith; and instead of hands, let praise offer it up to the Highest!

6.1: 1. Would that the memory of the fathers would exhale from the tombs; who were very simple as being wise, and reverend as believing. They without cavilling searched for, and came to the right path.
6.2: He gave the law; the mountains melted away; fools broke through it. By unclean ravens He fed Elijah at the desert stream; and moreover gave from the skeleton honey unto Samson. They judged not, nor inquired why it was unclean, why clean.
6.3: 2. And when He made void the sabbaths, the feeble Gentiles were clothed with health. Samson took the daughter of the aliens, and there was no disputing among the righteous; the prophet also took a harlot, and the just held their peace.
6.4: He blamed the righteous, [ Hosea 1:2 ] and He held up and lifted up [to view] their delinquencies: He pitied sinners, [ Matthew 9:13 ] and restored them without cost: and made low the mountains of their sins: [ Luke 18:9 ] He proved that God is not to be arraigned by men, and as Lord of Truth, that His servants were His shadow; and whatsoever way His will looked, they directed also their own wills; and because Light was in Him, [ Song of Songs 2:17 ] their shadows were enlightened.
6.5: 3. How strangely perplexed are all the heretics by simple things! For when He plainly foreshadowed this New Testament by that of the Prophets, those pitiable men rose, as though from sleep, and shouted out and made a disturbance. And the Way, wherein the righteous held straight on, and by their truths had gone forth therein, that [Way] have these broken up, because they were besotted: this they left and went out of; because they pried, an evil searching, [yea,] an evil babbling led them astray.
6.6: They saw the ray: they made it darkness, that they might grope therein: they saw the jewel, even the faith: while they pried into it, it fell and was lost. Of the pearl they made a stone, that they might stumble upon it.
6.7: 4. O Gift, which fools have made a poison! The People were for separating Your beauteous root from Your fountain, though they separated it not: [false] teachings estranged Your beauty also from the stock thereof.
6.8: By You did they get themselves estranged, who wished to estrange You. By You the tribes were cut off and scattered abroad from out of Sion, and also the [false] teachings of the seceders.
6.9: Bring Yourself within the compass of our littleness, O Gift of ours. For if love cannot find You out on all sides, it cannot be still and at rest. Make Yourself small, You Who is too great for all, Who comes unto all!
6.10: 5. By this would those who wrangle against our Pearl be reproved; because instead of love, strife has come in and dared to essay to unveil your beauty. It was not graven, since it is a progeny which cannot be interpreted.
6.11: You showed your beauty among the abjects to show whereto you are like, you Pearl that art all faces. The beholders were astonied and perplexed at you. The separatists separated you in two, and were separated in two by you, you that are of one substance throughout.
6.12: They saw not your beauty, because there was not in them the eye of truth. For the veil of prophecy, full as it was of the mysteries; to them was a covering of your glistering faces: they thought that you were other [than you are], O you mirror of ours! And therefore these blind schismatics defiled your fair beauty.
6.13: 6. Since they have extolled you too much, or have lowered you too much, bring them to the even level. Come down, descend a little from that height of infidelity and heathendom; and come up from the depth of Judaism, though you are in the Heaven.
6.14: Let our Lord be set between God and men! [ 1 Timothy 2:5 ] Let the Prophets be as it were His heralds! Let the Just One, as being His Father, rejoice! That Word it is which conquered both Jews and Heathens!
6.15: 7. Come, You Gift of Holy Church, stay, rest in the midst of Her! The circumcised have troubled You, in that they are vain babblers, and so have the [false] doctrines in that they are contentious. Blessed be He that gave You a goodly company which bears You about!
6.16: In the covenant of Moses is Your brightness shadowed forth: in the new covenant You dart it forth: from those first Your light shines even unto those last. Blessed be He that gave us Your gleam as well as Your bright rays.

7.1: 1. As in a race saw I the disputers, the children of strife, [trying] to taste fire, to see the air, to handle the light: they were troubled at the gleaming, and struggled to make divisions.
7.2: The Son, Who is too subtle for the mind, did they seek to feel: and the Holy Ghost Who cannot be explored, they thought to explore with their questionings. The Father, Who never at any time was searched out, have they explained and disputed of.
7.3: The sound form of our faith is from Abraham, and our repentance is from Nineveh and the house of Rahab, and ours are the expectations of the Prophets, [ Genesis 15:6 ] ours of the Apostles.
7.4: 2. And envy is from Satan: the evil usage of the evil calf is from the Egyptians. The hateful sight of the hateful image of four faces is from the Hittites. Accursed disputation, that hidden moth, is from the Greeks.
7.5: The bitter [enemy] read and saw orthodox teachings, and subverted them; he saw hateful things, and sowed them; and he saw hope, and he turned it upside down and cut it off. The disputation that he planted, lo! It has yielded a fruit bitter to the tooth.
7.6: 3. Satan saw that the Truth strangled him, and united himself to the tares, and secreted his frauds, and spread his snares for the faith, and cast upon the priests the darts of the love of pre-eminence.
7.7: They made contests for the throne, to see which should first obtain it. There was that meditated in secret and kept it close: there was that openly combated for it: and there was that with a bribe crept up to it: and there was that with fraud dealt wisely to obtain it.
7.8: The paths differed, the scope was one, and they were alike. Him that was young, and could not even think of it, because it was not time for him; and him that was hoary and shaped out dreams for time beyond; all of them by his craftiness did the wicked one persuade and subdue. Old men, youths, and even striplings, aim at rank!
7.9: 4. His former books did Satan put aside, and put on others: the People who was grown old had the moth and the worm devoured and eaten and left and deserted: the moth came into the new garment of the new peoples:
7.10: He saw the crucifiers who were rejected and cast forth as strangers: he made of those of the household, pryers; and of worshippers, they became disputants. From that garment the moth gendered and wound it up and deposited it.
7.11: The worm gendered in the storehouse of wheat, and sat and looked on: and lo! The pure wheat was mildewed, and devoured were the garments of glory! He made a mockery of us, and we of ourselves, since we were besotted!
7.12: He showed tares, and the bramble shot up in the pure vineyard! He infected the flock, and the leprosy broke out, and the sheep became hired servants of his! He began in the People, and came unto the Gentiles, that he might finish.
7.13: 5. Instead of the reed which the former people made the Son hold, others have dared with their reed to write in their tracts that He is only a Son of man.
